project_overview.name: CET - Corporate Entrance Test by Startup Times
project_overview.description: Official national entrance examination platform for Indian college final-year students and recent graduates. Designed to feel like a high-credibility national examination body (UPSC/CAT style trust) rather than a startup landing page.
project_overview.target_audience: Final-year undergraduate students, recent post-graduates, entry-level job seekers, corporate recruiters, and examination administrators across India.

brand_identity.visual_tone: Authoritative, Official, National-Scale Credibility, Editorial Precision, Corporate Trust.
anti_patterns: No playful startup illustrations or bouncy 3D cartoon avatars
No bright rainbow gradients or neon glowing cards
No center-aligned hero block with centered text everywhere
No transparent headers without backdrop blur or proper contrast over scrollable content
No default Inter for main section titles without proper weight and tracking
core_principles: UPSC / CAT / NTA Level Trust: Solid borders, structured data tables, clear exam schedules, official notice badges.

Dual Theme Structure: Clean crisp white/off-white background for information sections, and deep rich navy (#0F172A / #0A1128) for header, hero, and special spotlight sections (Dubai Global Experience, Closing CTA, Admin Navbar).
Single Accent Focus: Warm Amber / Gold (#F5A623) strictly used for CTAs, step active indicators, key callouts, and urgency badges.
Data Density with Breathers: High readability tables, clear timeline steps, generous card padding (p-6 to p-8), clear grid hierarchy.

instructions_to_main_agent: Ensure all 9+ public pages (Home, About, How It Works, Program, Dubai Experience, Employers, FAQs, Blog, Login, Apply, Dashboard, Admin) are fully accessible via the top navigation or footer links.

Strictly follow the color palette: White/Off-white background for body sections, Deep Navy (#0F172A) for header, hero, Dubai section, closing CTA, and Amber (#F5A623) as the single vibrant action color.
Ensure responsiveness on mobile, tablet, and desktop.
All interactive elements (buttons, inputs, filters, tabs, links, table actions) MUST have explicit data-testid attributes in kebab-case format.
Use Lucide icons for all UI elements (ShieldCheck, Award, FileText, Globe, Calendar, CheckCircle2, Building2, User, ArrowRight, Download, Search, ChevronDown, Lock, Clock).
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur) where appropriate.
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: transition: all. This results in breaking transforms. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add .App { text-align: center; } in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER: use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations. Static = dead.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
Main agent relies on these image URLs. Missing categories (especially sponsor logos) = main agent will use placeholder text which is FORBIDDEN.
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable.
Create new components that match the style and conventions of existing components when needed.
Examine existing components to understand the project's component patterns before creating new ones.
Use sonner for toasts. Sonner component is located in /app/src/components/ui/sonner.jsx or /app/frontend/src/components/ui/sonner.jsx.
